g.title: cluster_graph
g.text: nodes are S lines, arrows are links (L lines)
reference chr1 in blue; s5, an HG002 allele in place of s3, in orange

g.title: cluster_files
g.text: one row per node and one per link, each filed under a chr1 interval

g.title: cluster_query
g.text: one tabix request per file returns the rows filed over chr1:25-30

g.title: cluster_drawn
g.text: s2 and s4 come from the link rows

g.title: rows
g.text: s5 lies off chr1, so the tool files it under the
reference span it hangs from: s2 to s4, chr1:10-40.
The tool files a link under the span both its nodes reach, so a query near either node returns it.
The row gives both nodes' coordinates, so a reader places the far node without another query.

g.title: hits
g.text: returned, dropped: touches neither s3 nor s5
The reader keeps a link when the node file returned one of its nodes, or when both its nodes
are far ends of links it kept. s1→s2 fails both tests, since s1 is no kept link's far end.
